name: Ted Turner
role: Founder of CNN and Turner Broadcasting; philanthropist (UN Foundation, Nuclear Threat Initiative)
summary: A media executive turned philanthropist who spoke mainly on international cooperation, nuclear disarmament, population, the environment and media concentration. He backed the UN, nuclear abolition, smaller families, a shift from fossil fuels and breaking up large media conglomerates. His recorded views on most economic, social and cultural questions are thin.

nation-first.rationale: Told Kansas State that 'we are going to survive together or we're going to perish together' and, on NPR, that isolationism 'was good when we were a small country' but 'we're a superpower now, and we have to take our responsibility in the world, seriously, because if we don't do it, nobody else can'.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Said 'We have got to move away from fossil fuels and stop putting CO2 into the atmosphere'; warned in 2008 of catastrophe without action on global warming.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Listed wind, solar and biofuels and said 'possibly even expand nuclear power': a hedged, passing remark.

military-superiority.rationale: Called military budgets 'a big waste of time' and said 'the superpowers of tomorrow are not going to be the military powers of today' but the countries that invest in 'education, health care, science and technology'.

limit-population.rationale: Said 'We cannot keep piling billions and billions more people into a finite world' and that families must be smaller; in 2010 said China's one-child policy should be implemented, and funded population work through his foundation.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Said 'military conquest is no longer a good way to do things', citing Vietnam and Iraq.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Said we must move away from fossil fuels; in 2010 said 'maybe we ought to just leave the coal in the ground' and use solar, wind and geothermal.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Said 'we've got to abolish poverty', pointed to the UN Millennium goals and gave $1 billion to UN humanitarian work; no explicit statement of a duty of rich countries.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Said 'zero is best' for nuclear weapons and that all nuclear states should sign a treaty to get rid of them 'over a period of time' under IAEA supervision: 'If I was running the place, we would already be rid of them'.

ban-cartels.rationale: In his 2004 article called for new rules to break huge media companies apart, citing the breakup of the railroad trusts and Ma Bell; spoke about media, not all sectors.

arms-reduction.rationale: Called for cutting nuclear arsenals and ending hair-trigger alert, a treaty to get rid of nuclear weapons under IAEA supervision, and said military budgets are a big waste; co-founded the Nuclear Threat Initiative.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: At the launch of the Nuclear Threat Initiative he said 'I personally advocate the complete elimination of all weapons of mass destruction, including nuclear weapons, as quickly as possible. If fewer is better, then in my opinion, zero is best'; in Kansas he called for all eight nuclear powers to sign a treaty to get rid of theirs under IAEA supervision.

human-caused-global-warming.rationale: Named climate change as the second great danger and said 'we have got to move away from fossil fuels and stop putting CO2 into the atmosphere', treating emissions as the cause.

notes:
Wikipedia gives his death as 6 May 2026. Unreachable: unfoundation.org and nti.org (403), the NTI statement PDF (unreadable), NPR 2010 interview (timeout), Tampa Bay Times reprint (paywall). The 2008 Charlie Rose interview text was not opened, so the 'two children' remark is not used.

Read the 2005 Landon Lecture and his 2004 Washington Monthly article in full, the 2010 NPR interview and the 2001 CNN Nuclear Threat Initiative statement from the news corpus (CNN and NPR interviews 2000-2018 searched by theme). Six answers added (nuclear weapons, nation-first, military power, conquest, human-caused warming); the universal-healthcare answer rested only on Wikipedia and is nulled.
